question: What specific shielding materials and configurations are most effective in minimizing the spontaneous radiation emission of Antimony-122 during storage while maintaining compact storage dimensions?

items.requirement: Specification of a low-atomic-number (low-Z) material for the inner layer of shielding to stop beta particles from Antimony-122.
items.minimum_bar: The response must name at least one specific low-Z material suitable for beta shielding, such as aluminum or acrylic/plexiglass.
items.rationale: This is a core physical material required to construct the primary beta particle shield. It is a blocker because without it, Bremsstrahlung production would be unacceptably high.

items.requirement: Specification of a high-atomic-number (high-Z), high-density material for the outer layer of shielding to attenuate gamma rays and Bremsstrahlung from Antimony-122.
items.minimum_bar: The response must name at least one specific high-Z material suitable for gamma shielding, such as lead or tungsten.
items.rationale: This is a core physical material required to construct the gamma/X-ray shield. It is a blocker because low-Z materials are ineffective at stopping high-energy photons.

items.requirement: Identification of the specific radioisotope, Antimony-122, which is the source of the radiation to be shielded.
items.minimum_bar: The response must explicitly identify Antimony-122 (Sb-122) as the source of radiation whose properties dictate the shielding design.
items.rationale: This is the fundamental material being acted upon and is the absolute prerequisite for the task. It is a blocker because the entire shielding design depends on the properties of this specific isotope.

items.requirement: Description of the specific layered arrangement of shielding materials for a beta-gamma emitter like Antimony-122.
items.minimum_bar: The response must state that the low-Z material must be placed inside the high-Z material to shield the Antimony-122 source.
items.rationale: This describes the critical spatial arrangement of the materials, a core procedural step. It is a blocker because reversing the layers would be a critical design failure, increasing the secondary radiation hazard.

items.requirement: Specification of the method or principle used to calculate the required thickness of the gamma shielding material for Antimony-122.
items.minimum_bar: The response must mention using the Half-Value Layer (HVL) or Tenth-Value Layer (TVL) for the gamma energies of Antimony-122 to determine the required thickness.
items.rationale: This is a key procedural calculation needed to dimension the shield correctly for a desired level of attenuation. EVIDENCE
